title.value: Optimizing Deeper Transformers on Small Datasets
title.justification: The title of the paper is prominently mentioned at the top of the document, right after the list of authors and affiliations.
title.quote: Optimizing Deeper Transformers on Small Datasets

analysis.description: The paper demonstrates that with proper initialization and optimization, deep transformers can be effectively trained on small datasets, challenging the common belief that large datasets are essential for training such models from scratch. The authors propose a novel Data-dependent Transformer Fixed-update initialization scheme (DT-Fixup) and successfully train transformers on small datasets for Text-to-SQL semantic parsing and logical reading comprehension, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

type.justification: The paper involves experiments and benchmarks to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed initialization scheme, making it empirical in nature.
type.quote: In particular, we successfully train 48 layers of transformers, comprising 24 fine-tuned layers from pre-trained RoBERTa and 24 relation-aware layers trained from scratch. With fewer training steps and no task-specific pre-training, we obtain the state-of-the-art performance on the challenging cross-domain Text-to-SQL parsing benchmark Spider.

name.justification: The paper focuses on tasks such as Text-to-SQL semantic parsing and reading comprehension, which are subfields of Natural Language Processing.
name.quote: This work shows that this does not always need to be the case: with proper initial-ization and optimization, the benefits of very deep transformers can carry over to challenging tasks with small datasets, including Text-to-SQL semantic parsing and logical reading comprehension.

name.justification: The paper specifically evaluates the transformer models on the Spider benchmark, which is a Text-to-SQL parsing task.
name.quote: With fewer training steps and no task-specific pre-training, we obtain the state-of-the-art performance on the challenging cross-domain Text-to-SQL parsing benchmark Spider.

name.justification: The paper also evaluates the transformer models on the ReClor dataset, which focuses on logical reading comprehension.
name.quote: While Text-to-SQL semantic parsing is inherently different from reading comprehension, they share similar characteristics which require certain levels of reasoning and structural understanding ability.

name.quote: By applying DT-Fixup on different tasks, we show that the impression that deep transformers do not work on small datasets stems from the optimization procedure rather than the architecture. With proper initialization and optimization, training extra transformer layers is shown to facilitate the learning of complex relations and structures in the data.
